clue.text: Railing about lake or city in Italy

indicators.note: about means going around, so the railing word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a railing is a fence
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railed lakeside spot, or perhaps a famous Italian city, is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital, a city in Italy.

clue.text: Far from smart politician in terrible fury

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the scrambled letters of fury
terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of fury are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A badly dressed politician is in a fearful rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges fury, and 'in' houses the politician within those letters; 'Far from smart' means dowdy, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpy describes dowdy, unfashionable dress, the opposite of smart.

clue.text: 15's striking place

parts.note: workers on strike are said to be out
to lay something is to place it down

explanation.surface: A clue referring to another answer, a place where a strike happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is SPENDING, so the definition is 'spending'; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money laid out, an expenditure.

clue.text: Insists upon late turns

parts.note: late in the sense of former gives EX, as in an ex-wife
variety turns are acts on stage

explanation.surface: Someone insists on things arriving late in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand it and insist on receiving it.

clue.text: Using no scent — it's logical

indicators.note: using the letters suggests they are put to new work, rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: letters used as fodder
letters used as fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A fragrance-free choice is called the sensible one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is an unusual anagram signal: the ten letters of NO SCENT IT'S are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent reasoning holds together without contradiction, which makes it coherent and sound.

clue.text: A capacious vehicle a newspaper leader disparaged

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle carrying many passengers
ED is short for editor, the person leading a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is criticising a roomy vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like an editorial column; here it is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Abused here means insulted or spoken of with contempt, a synonym of disparaged.

clue.text: By no means finished trading

explanation.surface: Someone is described as not at all done with business.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankrupt person is without means to pay and is forced to stop doing business.

clue.text: Covered outbuilding to hold in the warmth

indicators.note: to hold in means the shed word encloses the other word

parts.note: a shed is a garden outbuilding
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A covered garden building keeps the warmth inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The warmth sits just after the first letter of the outbuilding; 'to hold in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathed means encased, as a sword is in its scabbard.

clue.text: One cannot recommend taking animals without examination

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the animals word surrounds the other

parts.note: deer are animals
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to recommend taking animals that have not been checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not 'lacking', so the animals go around the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A detester loathes something, so is the last person to recommend it.

clue.text: Puritans agitated for transport to town

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Puritans in a fluster are being carried into town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an up train is one heading towards the capital or a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: Up trains are railway services travelling towards London or the main city.

clue.text: Order during the depression

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: An order arrives in the middle of the economic depression.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is a formal requisition, a purchase request for goods.

clue.text: A fruit worker given flat accommodation

indicators.note: given accommodation means housed inside, so the flat word encloses the worker

parts.note: a plain is flat land
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A fruit picker is given a flat to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment; it is PLAIN, level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit, cooked before eating.

clue.text: Note the reprobate is priceless!

parts.note: G is a musical note
a rat is a contemptible, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a scoundrel is invaluable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priceless' suggests invaluable; here it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, with no price to pay.

clue.text: Top man not favouring a person going fishing

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a troller fishes by trailing a line behind a boat

explanation.surface: A boss is against an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: A controller is the person in charge, the chief who directs.

clue.text: The general feeling at doctors parking in this spot

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; MOS is plural
P is the standard sign abbreviation for parking
here means in this place

explanation.surface: General mood among doctors about parking at this location.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the prevailing mood or tone of a place or occasion.

clue.text: Starting price closing 2

parts.note: SP is the racing abbreviation for starting price, the final odds
a closing is an ending

explanation.surface: A clue linking a starting price to a closing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 2 down, OUTLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending is money laid out, the expenditure the other clue names.

clue.text: Criminal requiring a ship to get dope in

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship
a dope is a fool, an ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal needs a ship to smuggle drugs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs; here it is a fool, ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer of a prominent person, a murderous criminal.

clue.text: Relish with sage is provided in addition

parts.note: to relish is to like
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A relish flavoured with sage is supplied as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' and 'sage' look like a condiment and herb; here they are verb and adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means also, similarly, as well.

clue.text: Make paste, so in a mess, but enthusiastic

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters used as fodder
letters used as fodder
letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone making paste gets into a mess but stays keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' are fodder, not a link: PASTE SO IN A gives ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate means ardent and fervent, full of keen feeling.

clue.text: Work for periods on musical entertainments

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
eras are periods of time

explanation.surface: Work done over periods on musical shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged dramas set to music, a kind of sung show.

clue.text: Quietly increase credit

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a raise is an increase

explanation.surface: A discreet pay rise is credited.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit someone is to give them acclaim and commendation.

clue.text: Little is left in view

indicators.note: in puts the left letter inside the view word

parts.note: sight means view

explanation.surface: Only a little is left to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means small or slender, of minor size.

clue.text: A quarter scoffed when made to spruce up

parts.note: N, north, is one of the four compass quarters
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A quarter of something is eaten when someone tidies up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mocked; in British slang to scoff is to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to tidy, making things orderly.

clue.text: Personal serving man

explanation.surface: A personal servant is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means relating to the body, as in corporal punishment; a corporal is also a non-commissioned army officer, a soldier in service.

clue.text: Plant in almost complete calm

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the final letter of the calm word goes

parts.note: still means utterly calm

explanation.surface: Something planted in almost total tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to implant an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to implant it gradually in someone's mind.

clue.text: Marginal changes that can be quite daunting

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of the word marginal shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Even minor changes can be frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarming means frightening and disturbing, causing dismay.

clue.text: A bird to catch on horse-back

indicators.note: on means the catch word is placed after the reversed horse, in a down-or-across build
back means the horse word is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A bird is caught while riding on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse-back' reads as riding, but splits into the horse and 'back', the reversal signal; 'on' puts the catch after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large diving seabird of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: In tip-top environs chance being most energetic

indicators.note: environs means surroundings, so the top word goes around the chance word

parts.note: tip-top means the best
a risk is a chance

explanation.surface: Within a first-rate setting, risk-taking proves most lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskest means liveliest and quickest, the superlative of brisk.
